policy.tsx.questionsAboutSiteUsagePrivac: For questions about site usage or privacy, contact the author by email.
policy.tsx.siteProvidesIpLookupsNetworkD: This site provides IP lookups, network diagnostics, browser checks and service status queries. See the API page for API usage.
policy.tsx.useTheseToolsTargetsAuthorize: Use these tools only for targets you are authorized to test. Do not use the site for unlawful activity, disrupting third-party services, bypassing access restrictions or abusing the API.
policy.tsx.resultsDependNetworkBrowserRe: Results depend on the network, browser restrictions and third-party data. They are for reference and do not guarantee security, account access or continued availability. Maintenance, rate limits or upstream failures may interrupt service.
policy.tsx.whenVisitingThirdPartyLinksUs: When visiting third-party links or using their services, follow their terms as well. Use of the source code is governed by the license in the repository.
policy.tsx.hostingServiceProcessesReques: The hosting service processes your request IP and necessary network request information. IP and domain queries and network tests send the relevant target to the selected data source or diagnostic service. Third-party sites contacted directly by your browser can also see that connection’s egress IP.
policy.tsx.browserDiagnosticsReadDisplay: Browser diagnostics read and display the environment, fingerprint or permission information needed by the selected checks. The consistency page automatically starts local deep diagnostics. Some network checks and optional CAPTCHA features contact third-party services.
policy.tsx.siteStoresThemeLanguageNotice: This site stores theme, language, notice preferences and lookup history in the current browser. Lookup history includes recent successful queries and results; queried addresses may also appear in browser history. You can clear local data through your browser’s site data settings.
policy.tsx.ipHealthQueriesSendQueriedPub: IP health queries send the queried public IP to reputation sources such as ipapi.is, proxycheck.io, AbuseIPDB, ipwho.is and Team Cymru (DNS lookups). Other queries, maps, site resources and verification features process necessary request data through their respective services. Third-party and hosting data processing and log retention depend on their policies and actual configuration.
policy.tsx.apiRequiresKeyButRateLimitedR: The API requires no key but is rate-limited by request IP. Reduce request frequency after a 429 response; do not rotate IPs to bypass limits. Cross-site browser calls are restricted. The API page documents the public endpoint.
policy.tsx.httpResponsesLatencyDifferIcm: HTTP responses and latency differ from ICMP ping and do not establish AI login, chat or model access. An egress IP describes the route of that request only. IP reputation and browser anomalies alone do not prove abuse or identity spoofing.
policy.tsx.featuresDataSourcesRateLimits: Features, data sources and rate limits may change. Check the current instructions before use and verify important results through the relevant official service.
policy.tsx.ipLookupsMayContactIpwhoIpSbI: IP lookups may contact ipwho.is, IP.SB or ipify; IP health uses this site's aggregated reputation sources. Global ping sends targets and probe selections to Globalping; maps prefer Tianditu and fall back to OpenStreetMap when it is not configured or unavailable; service status reads providers’ public endpoints. Requests depend on the pages and checks you select.
policy.tsx.webrtcChecksConnectGoogleClou: WebRTC checks connect to Google and Cloudflare STUN services and may reveal an egress address different from web requests. Camera, microphone and location tests start when clicked and are controlled by browser permissions. Media permission tests close the stream immediately without recording audio or video. Revoke permissions in browser settings.
policy.tsx.whenConfiguredUsedCaptchaFeat: When configured and used, CAPTCHA features load Cloudflare Turnstile or Google reCAPTCHA. This site forwards verification tokens to the provider for validation. Those services also process device and network signals under their own policies.
policy.tsx.lookupHistoryKeepsLatest10Suc: Lookup history keeps the latest 10 successful queries and results per category in the current browser; clear site data to remove it. The server uses request IPs for rate limiting. Hosting configuration enables sampled logs; actual records and retention depend on deployment settings. Clearing browser data does not remove third-party or hosting records. Contact the author with the request time and feature for data questions.
policy.tsx.optionalPublicIpv4Ipv6Default: Optional public IPv4 / IPv6; defaults to request egress. Required locally.
policy.tsx.ipLocationIspAsnReputationSco: IP, location, ISP, ASN, reputation score and risk flags; unknown values are null.
policy.tsx.75100Good4574Moderate044: 75–100 good · 45–74 moderate · 0–44 poor; unknown when no score is available.
policy.tsx.jsonError400InvalidInput403Cr: JSON error: 400 invalid input · 403 cross-site request · 405 wrong method · 429 rate limit · 502 upstream failure · 503 specify an IP.
policy.tsx.netCoffeeDataIpReputationRefe: Scores come from this site's aggregated reputation sources and are for IP reputation reference. Browser calls must be same-origin. Retry later after rate limiting.
methodology.title: Methodology
methodology.description: How every score and verdict on this site is produced, in full
methodology.neutral1: We measure, we don't sell: no paid score changes or listings from airports or VPS sellers, no affiliate links.
methodology.neutral2: The code is open source (based on one-ip, AGPL-3.0); the verdict rules live in the repository for anyone to review.
methodology.purity1: Sources: ipapi.is, proxycheck.io, AbuseIPDB (keyed) plus Team Cymru, PTR, RPKI and geo databases (keyless).
methodology.purity2: Risk is the maximum of: Tor 90, proxy/compromised 85, AbuseIPDB confidence, ipapi abuser label (Elevated 15 / High 40 / Very High 75), VPN 50, proxycheck risk (only when it actually flags proxy/VPN), type baseline (datacenter 15, business 10, residential 0).
methodology.purity3: Adjustments: registry vs located country mismatch +5, RPKI invalid +10. Purity = 100 − risk.
methodology.purity4: Fewer than two working risk sources is shown as insufficient data. Purity describes how an IP is flagged; it does not guarantee a service such as Claude will accept it.
methodology.route1: Only backbone-prefix hops are counted, never the order of hop ASNs: provincial access routers also announce AS4134/AS4837 and are not backbone evidence. Prefixes verified against APNIC whois and RIPEstat (2026-11-05).
methodology.route2: Telecom: CN2 = 59.43.0.0/16, 163 backbone = 202.97.0.0/17. ≥2 CN2 hops with at most one user-side hand-over → CN2 GIA; ≥2 hops on 202.97 → CN2 GT; ≥2 163 hops on the server side after CN2 → mixed; 163 only → Telecom 163.
methodology.route3: Unicom: 9929 = 218.105.0.0/16, 210.51.0.0/16; 169 backbone = 219.158.0.0/17. 9929 needs ≥2 hops (both blocks contain IDC customer space); AS10099 without 9929 is ordinary Unicom international, not premium.
methodology.route4: Mobile: CMIN2 follows AS58807's announced subnets, other 223.118–121 space is CMI, 223.121.128.0/17 and 221.176.0.0/13 are CMNET. CMIN2 transit followed by ≥2 CMI hops to the server counts as CMI.
methodology.route5: Each measurement uses 3 eyeball/provincial probes per carrier (IDC probes excluded), 10 packets each, and records Beijing time. Disagreeing probes show “varies by province” at the worst tier seen.
methodology.route6: When the IP itself is in mainland China (domestic carrier or cloud), it is a domestic relay entry and no international route verdict is given.
methodology.direction1: The site measures the forward path (China → server) with GlobalPing China probes. Downloads use the return path (server → China); the two are often asymmetric.
methodology.direction2: The return path can only be measured on the server: run nexttrace / backtrace on the node and paste the output into the return-route card on the IP page; the same rules classify it.
methodology.direction3: Latency and loss on forward results come from round trips and include return-path quality, but cannot name the return line.
methodology.split1: Proxy clients route by destination domain, so the browser requests each service's own domain and reads the visitor IP it echoes.
methodology.split2: Exits are readable on Cloudflare-fronted sites (/cdn-cgi/trace), AWS checkip and a few Chinese CDNs. YouTube, Netflix, Telegram, GitHub, Apple and others do not echo the visitor IP; only reachability can be checked.
methodology.split3: Sites whose exit lands in mainland China are treated as direct (a DIRECT rule matched).
methodology.airport1: Subscriptions are parsed in the browser and credentials are dropped during parsing; entry identification uses public DoH (Cloudflare / Google) from the browser, so entry IPs never pass through this site's server.
methodology.airport2: Entries fall into domestic relay (in mainland), premium line (CN2/CMI/9929 carrier networks or line hosts), CDN proxy and direct overseas. Airports whose entries are mostly the first two are relay-line airports.
methodology.airport3: Nodes named IPLC/private line/relay whose entry is a CDN or direct overseas host are flagged as misrepresented. Exit (landing) IPs can only be checked on the home page after connecting to a node.
methodology.cost1: Datacenter tiers come from the site's catalog (ASN → brand → tier); route premium comes from the carrier verdicts. Price ranges are rough public list prices for reference only.
methodology.cost2: Plans priced far below the cost range warrant caution about overselling or the seller disappearing.
methodology.limits1: A single forward measurement depends on which probes are chosen; the same IP can read differently with other probes. Repeat at evening peak for reliability.
methodology.limits2: IPLC/IEPL private lines are invisible on the public internet; from outside we can only confirm the entry is domestic, not prove a private line.
methodology.limits3: The datacenter catalog covers about 50 providers; others show only ASN and registry name.
